issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method signature does not match the specification and the solution: the template defines findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) but other methods in the template (e.g., add and take) call findStockIngredient(String) with a single parameter. The UML and the solution expect a single-argument findStockIngredient(String). This mismatch will cause compilation errors in the template and confuses students about which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Stock class provide the single-argument method findStockIngredient(String) as specified in the UML and used in other methods (or add an overloaded single-arg variant). Update any calls to match the chosen signature so the template compiles and matches the specification and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradiction about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section instructs students to create a final (instance) Stock field initialized in the constructor, while a later note explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and that acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice be static as well. This inconsistency can confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field or a static/shared field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement to consistently specify that the stock attribute is shared across all SealSaloon instances (declare it static final) and that related methods (acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice) are static. Remove or update any wording that implies stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor so students implement the intended static/shared design.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method (single String parameter), but the template repository's Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with an extra boolean parameter. This discrepancy creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem will look for a single-argument method and may be confused by the extra parameter in the starter code (or try to call the single-argument version and find it missing).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method to match the problem and solution by providing public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (single-argument), or add an overloaded single-argument version that delegates to the existing two-argument implementation. This aligns the template with the problem description and solution.
